name: Machine Downtime & OEE Intelligence – Six Big Losses, AI Agent RCA & Auto Work Orders

parameters.content:
## 🏭 Machine Downtime & OEE Intelligence

For plant heads and maintenance leads in small and mid-size factories who still run OEE in a spreadsheet days after the shift, when nobody remembers why line 3 stopped. This calculates it within minutes of every shift and turns the worst losses into work orders.

### How it works
Operators log output, scrap and downtime per machine through a form, or a PLC/IoT gateway posts it to a webhook. Fifteen minutes after each shift, OEE is calculated per machine and losses are split into the TPM Six Big Losses, with anomalies flagged against a 7-day baseline.

An AI agent looks at each critical machine's history and past maintenance tickets to find patterns, including repeat failures after a repair. The plant head gets a WhatsApp report with a Pareto chart, KPIs are logged, and critical machines get a work order (or their open ticket is updated) with a WhatsApp escalation to maintenance.

### Setup steps
1. Create a Google Sheet with **Machine Master**, **Shift Log**, **OEE History** and **Maintenance Tickets** tabs.
2. Connect Google Sheets, OpenAI and WhatsApp Business Cloud. Add Header Auth for the IoT webhook.
3. Replace `REPLACE_WITH_…` values, then set phone numbers, OEE target and shift times in **Identify Completed Shift**.
4. Log one test shift, run the schedule once manually, then activate.

## 📝 Shift Data Capture
Operators log output, scrap and downtime per machine through the form, or a PLC/IoT gateway posts the same data to the webhook. Entries are validated and upserted, so a resubmission corrects the row instead of duplicating it.

nodes.name: Sticky Note – Shift Close & Data Load

parameters.content:
## ⏰ Shift Close & Data Load
Runs 15 minutes after each shift ends (06:15, 14:15, 22:15 IST), works out which shift just closed, and loads the machine master and shift log.

## 📊 OEE Engine
Calculates Availability, Performance, Quality and OEE per machine, splits losses into the Six Big Losses, and flags anomalies against the 7-day baseline. If nobody logged the shift, the plant head is told instead.

nodes.name: Sticky Note – AI Root-Cause Agent & Report

parameters.content:
## 🧠 AI Root-Cause Agent & Report
The agent checks each critical machine's OEE history and past tickets to spot trends and repeat failures after repair, then returns assignable actions. Its output becomes a WhatsApp report and a Pareto chart.

## 📲 Report & History Log
The plant head gets the shift report and Pareto chart on WhatsApp. Every machine's KPIs are added to OEE History, which the agent reads next time.

## 🛠️ Work Orders & Escalation
For each critical machine, an open ticket is updated if one exists; otherwise a new work order is created. Once all are processed, maintenance gets one WhatsApp escalation.

## 🔐 Credentials & Security
Protect the IoT webhook with Header Auth and keep the token out of the gateway's public config. Store Sheets, OpenAI and WhatsApp keys as credentials. The Pareto chart is rendered by quickchart.io, so it only carries machine names and minutes.

options.systemMessage:
You are a senior manufacturing reliability engineer (TPM, OEE, RCM).
Goal: find ROOT-CAUSE PATTERNS behind this shift's losses, not just restate the numbers.

How to work:
1. Start from the largest of the Six Big Losses and the critical machines.
2. For each critical or anomalous machine, call the "OEE History" tool to inspect its longer trend.
3. For each critical machine, call the "Maintenance Tickets" tool. If a ticket was recently closed and the same failure is back, mark repeat_after_repair = true and recommend a deeper fix (RCA or 5-Why, a spare part, a PM interval change) instead of another quick repair.
4. Separate the loss types: speed loss (Performance), stoppages (Availability) and scrap (Quality).
5. Give actions that are specific and assignable (who, what, by when) and can start next shift.
Use only the data and tool results. Never invent sensor readings or ticket IDs. Keep it concise because this goes to WhatsApp.
